audioDescription: Silent. No audio track. Authored visual cue sequence: phrase beats at 0, 0.12, 0.38, 0.55 and 0.82 s; re-weight at 1.2 s; T swap at 1.55 s; lintel morph at 1.56 and 1.86 s with amber fill from 1.6 s; words land 1.95 to 2.14 s; tagline at 2.2 and 2.32 s; hold from 2.6 s.
limitations: No variable font file is bundled. The weight axis uses the macOS system UI font (system-ui / SF, which has a variable wght axis) through CSS font-weight. On a renderer without that font, the Helvetica Neue/Arial fallback steps between static weights instead of interpolating.

Font-to-path conversion (e.g. opentype.js) is not in the pool. The structural 'T' is an authored outline: two rectangles whose stem and crossbar positions come from a pixel scan of the rendered system-font T at weight 900. It is a close approximation, not an extracted glyph outline.
Only the T's crossbar (lintel) is deformed by MorphSVGPlugin, and only the stem rect is lengthened. All other glyphs stay live DOM text with intact counters.
The DOM T is swapped for the SVG T in one frame at 1.55 s at measured identical geometry. Subpixel antialiasing differences may be faintly visible for one frame.
Font size, weight and tracking are animated through CSS custom properties, so text reflows during those changes. Word position moves use only x/y transforms.
Architectural roles (lintel, support, load, aperture, platform) are an illustrative typographic approximation, not a physical simulation. The bend in the lintel is authored, not computed.

Palette: the background policy is scene_dependent, so the recipe source palette #102820 / #F4E9D5 / #F2B544 is adopted explicitly for this refresh. The earlier #FAF5E9 / #252D39 / #B84F3F was an example swatch. Amber marks 'system.' and the load-bearing T.
The light on the ground is a stationary CSS radial gradient (8% cream) plus a CSS grid. It is a flat approximation of a soft light source, not computed lighting.
Blender was not used, as instructed. Only HTML/CSS, SVG, GSAP and MorphSVGPlugin (all local) are used.
Source-frame evidence covers sampled seconds only, from three reviewed contact sheets.
